citations.quote: UOW ranks 6th in the world for Philosophy in QS Subject Rankings 2026
Curtin ranked fourth in the world for Mineral and Mining Engineering in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026.
Curtin is ranked in the top one per cent of universities worldwide in the highly regarded Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU) 2025.
Ranked 7th in the world — and 2nd in Australia — for reducing inequality (SDG 10)
RMIT also ranked 1st in Australia and 29th globally in Library & Information Management, an interdisciplinary subject area that spans data science, knowledge management and information science.

In the latest QS World University Rankings by Subject, UQ maintained its position as first nationally and 2nd globally for sports-related subjects for the 6th year, and rose to 5th globally for mineral and mining engineering.
Sports-related subjects reached their highest-ever rank, climbing 18 places to 29 to enter the world’s top 50, rising from ninth to fifth place in Australia.
The accolade marks the sixth time Deakin has topped the list globally, with wins in 2016 and 2017 and consecutive wins in 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024.
The University of Melbourne is the only Australian university to have ranked in the top 50 in all broad subject areas in 2025.
A total of 22 subjects were rated in the global top 100, a remarkable result in the first year of the institution.
A total of 42 ANU subjects are now ranked among the world’s best, contributing another four with this prestigious status.
Sports-related subjects jumped to 49, after being ranked 51-100 in 2025.
Among the subjects ranked, Architecture and Built Environment now places among the top 200 in the world, up from the top 240 in 2024.
In total, 39 UNSW subjects placed in the global top 100, with rankings based on academic reputation, employer reputation and research citations.
UTS was placed between 51st and 100th in the world for a further 12 subjects.
